courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Social Media Analytics
courses.description:
More than three-quarters of the top 100 companies are using at least one social media platforms (i.e., Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, etc). Definitely, social media marketing has emerging as a tectonic shift from traditional marketing.
This course introduces concepts, theories and applications of social network and social media analysis such as network and graph theory applications in social media, as well as network marketing and social media strategy. Through lecture, discussion, guest speakers, case studies and team project, students will come to evaluate how social media has changed the marketing paradigm and practices and many companies are struggling with it.
This course helps students implement social media strategies which involve different aspects of marketing and hone their network analytical skills. Due to a strong need for marketing professionals who are attuned to this area, this course is specifically for students who are planning to enter digital/social media marketing, consulting and brand management roles.
courses.learning_outcomes:
In this course, we will focus on the following:
1. "Social network" is way more than just terminologies and vocabularies. It includes key principles of Psychology and Sociology. Students will be able to master concepts and theories of social networks.
2. Social media is heavily technology driven. After taking this course, students will acquire techniques to statistically analyze social network data.
3. This course helps students design and develop marketing strategies based on social network analysis. Students will be able to apply social network analysis to marketing problems (i.e., advertising, segmentation, valuation, targeting, positioning, etc) and measure effectiveness of the social network marketing strategies.

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Behavioral Decision Making and Consumer Choice
courses.description: We are all consumers. As consumers, we make decisions every day, from the trivial to the fundamental. Psychologists and behavioral scientists in the related fields have studied how people process information and make decisions individually and in a group. This course is devoted to understanding how a consumer decides and judges in daily consumption contexts. Topics to cover include mental blocks and fixations, decision heuristics, behavioral nudge, motivated reasoning, affective influences, group decision making, etc.. This course will help the students discover a series of serious yet often overlooked mistakes that most consumers would commit in various consumption contexts. At the same time, this course will also teach students how to correct these mistakes and how to utilize such knowledge in crafting marketing tactics (e.g., pricing, advertising) to influence consumers’ choice and behavior.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To help the students understand the nature, causes and managerial implications of consumer decision pitfalls.

2. To teach the students how to correct mistakes that arise from the process and how to apply the knowledge to influence consumers' decisions.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Fundamental process in thinking and judgments: Sensation and perception and human judgments

2. Higher level process in thinking and judgments: mental blocks and fixation versus creative solutions

3. Heuristic approach to thinking

4. Behavioral nudge and its applications in marketing contexts

5. Motivated reasoning and judgments

6. Affective influence and its implications in marketing contexts

7. Groupthink, group polarization, and biases in group decisions

8. Behavioral perspective on marketing strategy

courses.description: The objective of this course is to give students advanced practical marketing research techniques as well as hands-on experience in solving marketing problems in the real-world environment. The course consists of some lectures on advanced but practical marketing research techniques and a group project. In the group project, students will work closely with the marketing manager of a firm to solve his or her marketing problem(s) by using primary marketing research. Students will need to do presentation to the firm’s marketing and/or management team as well as submitting a detailed written report or marketing plan.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc in Marketing
courses.learning_outcomes: Upon the completion of the course, students will acquire the knowledge and skills in problem formulation, research design, data collection, data analysis, data interpretation, and marketing planning needed to solve a marketing problem in a real-life situation. Specifically, students will be able to effectively handle marketing problems for products in different stage of the product life cycle (e.g., new product concept testing in the introductory stage and growth stage and positioning research/perceptual mapping for the maturity stage) as well as for problems in different marketing functions such as advertising testing and pricing testing.

courses.recommended_readings: To be assigned by course teacher

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Practicum in AI and Quantitative Marketing
courses.description: This course adopts an applied approach that integrates marketing concepts and analytics with hands-on experience in a real-world business setting. Given the opportunity of conducting different consulting projects from the sponsorship of client organizations, students learn how to apply the knowledge and data analytics tools learned from lessons and address big data marketing challenges and problems faced by international and regional businesses. Students will work in teams, under the supervision of project supervisors, to conduct consulting studies for the client organizations. This practicum addresses the clients’ strategic marketing issues and business needs, and provides insightful analyses and recommendations that guide marketing decision making and innovation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc in Marketing
courses.learning_outcomes: Upon the completion of the course, students will understand how to integrate data, IT and business as solutions to big data marketing problems. In addition, they will acquire the knowledge in data cleansing, data integration and data modeling. They learn the big data software and improve their IT skills.
courses.course_syllabus:

3. Project implementation (7 weeks)
4. Project presentation (1 week)

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Marketing - Behavioral Studies II
courses.description: This seminar covers major behavioral decision making related issues in behavioral marketing. It is focused on the selected current theory and research in areas of contemporary importance and relevance to behavioral decision making. Topics will vary over course offerings but may include heuristics and biases, prospect theory, mental accounting, preference construction, etc.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will acquire an in-depth understanding of theoretical and empirical issues in the area and potential areas for further exploration.

courses.description: Review of basic processes underlying consumer judgements and decisions. Topics include knowledge accessibility, comprehension memory, inference and evaluation, and decision-making.

courses.title: Advanced Social Psychology for Business Research
courses.description: This course is designed to survey the major theories and research in understanding human behaviors in social contexts. In the first two weeks, students will be required to learn about or re-familiarize themselves with classic theories and research in social psychology. In the remainder of the course, students will learn major theories that guide contemporary research in social psychology and how the theories can be used to generate novel hypotheses in business studies.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For MPhil/PhD students of Faculty of Business Administration
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of this course, students (1) should have acquired knowledge of major theories and methods in micro-level analysis of business behaviors, (2) will con-sider psychological variables in research, and (3) can generate psychological ex-planations in their own research.

Social identity theories

courses.subject: MKTG
courses.title: Advanced Cultural Psychology for Business Research
courses.description: This course focuses on cultural influences on behaviors in business settings (marketing, management, financial decision making, and business ethics). We will first survey major cultural theories, and then discuss major cross-cultural differences revealed in self, attribution and social inferences, thinking and perceptual styles, emotion, and motivation. The aim is to understand how culture impacts business behaviors and how Asians may differ from individuals from other cultural background. This knowledge will lay a strong foundation for students to formulate business research in an emerging Asian Century.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For MPhil/PhD students of Faculty of Business Administration
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of this course, students should be able to (1) appreciate cultural influences on human psychology and behaviors, (2) understand scientific examination of cultural influences, and (3) consider culture as a variable in their research.

courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Marketing - Analytical Models
courses.description: This seminar course emphasizes on analytical modeling methods in marketing studies. It will cover a wide range of topics including consumer search models, marketing-mix models, competitive marketing strategies, behavioral industrial organization, and research advances in e-marketing. The course will also introduce some basic analytical tools from areas of decision science, economics, and statistics.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Marketing; or MPhil-PhD Decisions, Operations and Technology; or MPhil-PhD Decision Sciences and Managerial Economics
courses.learning_outcomes:
Advanced Seminar in Marketing-Analytical Models aims to explore analytical modeling techniques in marketing studies. By the end of this course, students should be able to master logic and basic tools in analytical modeling, understand how to implement them as well as how to interpret results. Understanding how to incorporate analytical tools with marketing research questions is the essence, while learning relevant analytical and quantitative methods is necessary for conducting rigorous marketing research.
